subject: Sealed-media update handoff and offline image verification
messages:
From: Jordan Keats <ops@medcore.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: sealed-media update for air-gapped deployment

Hi Laura,

We're preparing an offline update of the MedCore on-prem inference cluster (production VPC, fully air-gapped). We need Redwood's sign-off and a handoff plan for shipping the OS image + model artifacts on sealed media.

High-level: we will receive an encrypted USB package from your team, verify signatures, import images into our offline registry, and run the scheduled maintenance window. Please confirm:
- Recommended signing format (GPG/PKCS7) and whether we should expect an ASC signature + detached manifest.
- File naming and manifest fields you require for audit (checksum, build id, model hash).
- Your recommended courier and chain-of-custody checklist (we can use Secure Logistics if you approve).

Attached: manifest_v1.csv (initial artifact list).

Target window: week of Dec 20 (flexible).

Thanks,
Jordan Keats
Ops Lead – MedCore Health Systems

Attachment: manifest_v1.csv (3 rows: image_name, sha256, build_id)

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Jordan Keats <ops@medcore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: sealed-media update for air-gapped deployment

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary. Happy to run this with you. A few clarifying items from our side so we can lock the runbook:

1) Signing format: we use GPG detached signatures (.asc) for images and a signed JSON manifest. We can do PKCS7 if your team prefers; please confirm.
2) Manifest fields we require: artifact_name, artifact_type (image/model), sha256, build_tag, signer_key_id, timestamp, expiration.
3) HSM/KMS: We sign artifacts in our HSM and will provide a signed-manifest.asc. If you need to verify against your own PKI, we can export our public verification key.
4) Transport: Secure Logistics is acceptable. We will provide a tamper-evident tamper-seal ID and a signed pickup manifest.

I'll drop an internal checklist (update_requirements.md) and loop in Dev and Security to confirm verification scripts and rollback behavior. Can you confirm whether MedCore requires an encrypted container (LUKS) for the USB or if signature-only is sufficient?

Next steps:
- Dev: propose verification commands and automated checks.
- Marissa: confirm compliance items and any additional audit evidence.
- Jordan: confirm physical transport encryption preference.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Deployments | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Confidential

Attachment: update_requirements.md

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jordan Keats <ops@medcore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: sealed-media update for air-gapped deployment

Quick technical notes on verification and a proposed minimal runbook excerpt: 

- We will deliver: image.tar.gz, model_v3.bin, signed-manifest.asc (detached GPG).
- Verification sequence (recommended):
  1) Verify GPG signature: gpg --verify signed-manifest.asc manifest.json
  2) Validate manifest entries against local sha256 sums: sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
  3) Ensure build_tag matches approved release (release tags are documented in the manifest).
  4) Import to air-gapped registry only after verification.

- We will provide a lightweight verify-script.sh (attached) that performs steps 1–3 and exits nonzero on mismatch.
- If MedCore prefers PKCS7, we can emit both formats.
- Rollback: keep the previous image in the offline registry with a retained label "previous" and verify a smoke-test image before traffic cutover.

I'll attach signing-keys-proposal.txt and verify-script.sh for your review.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Lead Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: signing-keys-proposal.txt, verify-script.sh

Hi all — adding security/compliance items. TL;DR we need HSM-signed manifests, tamper-evident receipts, auditable chain-of-custody, and a post-deployment evidence bundle.

Mandatory items before we sign-off:
- Signed-manifest.asc from Redwood HSM (include signer_key_id and certificate chain).
- Tamper-evident seal ID recorded at pickup and drop-off. Seal must be single-use and listed on the manifest.
- Courier background check: vendor must provide ATO/contract and insurance; Secure Logistics has a standing vouch but we need a shipment-level attestation PDF.
- Evidence bundle post-update: verification logs, "sha256 verified" outputs, final registry snapshot, and digital receipts. Pack these into a single signed artifact for MedCore audit.

Temporary mitigations accepted: if MedCore mandates LUKS encryption on the USB we accept a LUKS header + passphrase exchange via a separate Docusign-protected envelope.

Attached: coc_checklist.pdf (chain-of-custody template), hsm_integration_notes.docx

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
